utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. I see that all counsel and accused have found a way to this courtroom rather to the courtroom announced. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Ms. Mahindaratne, there was matter to be raised, I understood.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It is with regard to two documents which were tendered on Friday by the Defence, document number D192. Now, at the time, Mr. President, I was following the English version on the e-court, and I did not have, unfortunately, time to scrutinize the original document. But after adjournment, when I looked at the original document, it appeared that the document doesn't have a seal. It has no signature. And considering the other military documentation which has been tendered in evidence so far by the Defence, as well as the Prosecution, this document somehow does not seem to conform to the ordinary military documents. So I just wanted to underscore that and point out to you that there is a problem with this document. However, we have not objected to its admission. I don't know whether it is appropriate now to ask Court to have it marked for identification. If that is not possible, I could also demonstrate the discrepancies through the examination, so that Court will give necessary weight at the appropriate stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Defence on this matter. It is just about D192?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: First, I regret that this wasn't raised over the weekend or some point in time to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- address the matter. To me, from what I can see in the e-court, the third page does not appear to be uploaded. I will, during the break, attempt to upload the third page to satisfy Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, if you find a seal in the signature on the third page, then we'll hear from you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I'm sorry. I didn't realise there was, because in both versions there was no third page. This is why -- I'm sorry if that is the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's do the following. A complete document will be uploaded; you look at it; if you have any further questions, you first put them to Mr. Misetic; and if Mr. Misetic does not come up with an answer that satisfies you, you always can raise the matter in -- I mean, whether you draw your attention to it or whether it will be in re-examination or whether you will try to change the status again from admitted into evidence to marked for identification. We'll then see how you proceed. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, one other point. May I request the Defence to tender D191 in its entirety. That's the personnel record of the witness; and I believe, considering the issues that were raised on Friday, his personnel record in its entirety would be relevant to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I may have a moment, Your Honour, to have a look at D191.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That is the personnel record. At the moment, there is only five pages, just excerpts, tendered in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, this was not discussed with me over the weekend, so I need some time to review exactly what the issue is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It's D190. I beg your pardon. I made a mistake. It's the personnel file of the witness. It's the last document on the list that was send by you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The original is for me, an eight-page document, Ms. Mahindaratne. At least, that is how it appears in e-court. I have to look at the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe we tendered everything that was in D190, so I'm not sure what the issue is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you explain, Ms. Mahindaratne, because in the English, I also find an eight-page document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, since this was -- this is the personnel record of witness's military service, I presume that there are the details of his -- the day he joined, the day he left; whereas, this document only has the disciplinary measures and just this letter sent to the 4th Guards Brigade. So I presume there would be many pages in this document; but if the Defence says that is all there is to it, then I take it that this is the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, this is the kind of information you often find in what is, I think, called the military booklet, or something, the document the soldier takes with him all the time wherever he goes. It is always open for you to ask in re-examination, or to ask him to give a full description of all periods of actual service. So I leave it at this moment to you. D192 still to be considered. Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I think we're talking about D190.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, D190. At this moment, I do not see how to complete an eight-page document, unless, of course, there is more, but you say this is all you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I would have to go back and look. I would say, Your Honour, this is a matter of principle. I mean, the Prosecution is able to obtain documents, just like we are. This is -- D190 is the documents we selected to tender into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It seems to be a series of documents of which the handwritten note --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Every document that is in D190 was tendered by us into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And Ms. Mahindaratne asked herself, since these documents are put together whether, this series is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: They were compiled but you see as separate documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... compiled by you as documents. So they are not part of a series. That was provided to you as a series.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct. We compiled them and put them into one exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This may be a selection of military documents, then you can make your own selection, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you ready to continue your cross-examination, Mr. Misetic. Then could Mr. Gojanovic be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Gojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony; that is, that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Misetic will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Misetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, please. Due to the special circumstances, please allow me to address you. The life of my family in Sibenik is currently under great media, social, and political pressure. The police are guarding my family around the clock. For that reason, before counsel Mr. Misetic continues his examination, in view of the fact that my honour and my dignity as a witness and as a person are under attack, please allow me, before this session proceeds, to present to you documents related to this case which indisputably corroborate my statement about my presence in the brigade and in this Operation Storm itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, have you given these documents to the Office of the Prosecutor at any earlier stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could not have given these documents earlier, because they have never been asked of me, since I am under oath and fully aware of my responsibility. Over the days that I was absent from this courtroom, I have not discussed my evidence in this case with anyone. The person who is accompanying me has given me these documents obtained through the operative team of our association, so that I can defend my honour and my dignity in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether your honour and dignity was attacked or whether you were presented with documents which give a different view on what had happened is still to be seen, but let's be very practical. I suggest that they, these documents, will be provided to the parties, so that they can have a look at it; and, of course, the Defence has different interests from Prosecution, but both parties can see to what extent they would like to use these documents during the further examination. Is that an acceptable procedure, Ms. Mahindaratne?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay. He is hidden behind Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is literally not meant in any way other way. Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we are agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would please provide these document to the usher, the usher will take care that both parties can have a look at it, because in the system of the Tribunal, it's primarily the parties who adduce evidence and assist the Chamber in understanding your testimony. However, the Chamber reserves its position. If neither party wants to use these documents, then we will consider whether or not we'll call for these documents anyhow, because the witness says they are relevant. So, Mr. Usher, would you please get the relevant documents from Mr. Gojanovic. Mr. Gojanovic, you've got them there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may kindly ask to make one copy for me, so that I may have them in further proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, it would be appreciated if, at least for the time being, you would leave originals, if they are originals, with us. Certainly, a copy will be made. I see it is quite a bundle of documents. Mr. Usher, perhaps, let's start by making three sets of copies. Yes, Mr. Gojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I am far away from home, giving evidence here in the Netherlands, I stated a moment ago that I bear full material and moral responsibility for these documents which are authentic and identical to the original which is kept at my home. Since I was not able to bring originals, I am producing copies here, and I leave it to the Court to verify the authenticity that is the identical nature of these copy to the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, let me first address the parties. I'm inclined to issue an order to Mr. Gojanovic to keep the originals in the state as they are at this moment, so that can with be produced at any later stage if there's any need to verify the authenticity of the documents. Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. First of all, copies will be made of these documents immediately, four sets of documents, so that all parties have a copy available. Of course, I don't know you, I take it they are in B/C/S. But the party will find their way to get a first impression. Of course, we will see whether in those circumstances, after the first session, we can release the witness from his duties. That's still to be seen. Perhaps, we should take a bit more time for that. Mr. Misetic, is it about the order?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to put on the record that I'm sure the court will allow us the opportunity to look at the documents and reserve a right to cross-examine on the documents, if we feel there is a need to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether that would be cross-examination, these documents come up in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Right. Obviously, we allow rules to allow the Defence to review documents and prepare in advance to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, we never can exclude from the possibility that the witness comes up with documents suddenly. But, as I said before, it might be a reason not to release the witness after the first session, but ask him to stay until you have had an opportunity to at least have look at these documents. Mr. Gojanovic, you've told us that of the documents you've given to the usher now, and which are being reproduced at this moment and of which you will get your set of copies back, you told us that the originals are at your home. Is that true for all of these documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That is true of all these documents, except one, which is the letter of Chief Prosecutor Carla Del Ponte addressed to the association. That letter is kept with the association. The other documents are of a personal nature, and they are a military secret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since the Chamber might need those documents at a later stage, the Chamber instructs you, therefore gives you an order, that you should keep these documents as they are now, and to make them available at first request to this Trial Chamber in order to have an opportunity to verify the authenticity of the documents of which you provided copies to us now. Is that understood? Mr. Misetic, you please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Gojanovic.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: With respect to what you've just told the Court, could you tell the Court the name of the person you are contacting in order to obtain these documents.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not I who contacted that gentleman. It's my escort. He contacted me. His name is Ivica Petric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And what did Mr. Petric tell you over the weekend?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How did you know that he had documents for you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: When he turned the documents over to you, did he say anything?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said these are your documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, you just told the Court earlier that they came from the operative team of your association. How do you know that the documents come from your operative team?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so because the documents bear the marking HUR BDV; and since I know hour our system functions in practice, I suppose that that was the procedure through which they were obtained.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So, because you didn't have a conversation with Mr. Petric, you don't know for a fact where these documents actually come from. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. The fact is that I know my personal documentation, and I suppose that it was my wife who gave these documents to the operative team of the association and that they were forwarded to Ivica Petric. So that's my assumption for which I have no confirmation. Nobody told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Returning to the -- your witness statement from 2005, going back to paragraph 10 of your statement. Towards the middle of the paragraph, you describe: "... another very good soldier, a citizen of Serbian ethnicity who was in our army. I began checking the military warehouse, but we found no other enemy soldiers." Then on Friday, in cross-examination, at page 2990, lines 21 to 23, you identified this soldier of Serbian ethnicity as having the last name Despot. I'd like to show you a statement given by Mr. Despot this weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I could ask, Mr. Registrar, for 1D -- I'm sorry. It is not in e-court yet because the statements came over the weekend, so we will be using Sanction. The document number is 1D22-0380. Mr. Usher, we have hard copies of the Croatian version of the statement, if we could give it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You note on the first page, Mr. Gojanovic, the statement is by Ratko Despot. You note his ethnic origin and his religion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If you turn the page, please. Sorry. Just for the record, the statement was taken 16 May 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 3, Mr. Despot says: "Prior to Operation Storm, I volunteered in the 1st Infantry Battalion of the 113th Sibenik Brigade as an intelligence officer, which was then transferred to Pavasovici and tasked with attacking over the Pozare mountain towards Sonkovic, Bratiskovici? And further down in paragraph five, second sentence says: "In the evening, I'm not sure what hour, the seven of us - the late Zivko Baric, Milenko Zivkovic, Tihomir Mis, and Josip Elez, two conscripts, and myself - entered the village of Djevrska. It might have been around 2100 hours." Paragraph 6: "I'm sure that Vladimir Gojanovic was not with us. I knew my personnel well, especially those that went with me." And then in paragraph 12: "During the operation, Vladimir Gojanovic was not a member of my unit." Now, I'm going to ask you just a question on this incident regarding spending the night in Djevrska. Before I do that, let me show you the second statement that we obtained over the weekend, which is from Mr. Mis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is also going to be shown on Sanction, with a hard copy to the witness, Mr. Usher. The document ID is 1D22-0388 -- I`m sorry, 1D22-0402. You'll note, on the cover page, it is the statement of Tihomir Mis, taken 18 May 2008. If we can turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 2: "During Operation Storm, I was a non-commissioned officer of the 2nd Company of the 1st Infantry Battalion of the 113th Infantry Brigade." Paragraph 6: "As a company non-commissioned officer, I knew all members of the company, as this was the duty of a company non-commissioned officer. Paragraph 7: "On 5 August 1995, before night-fall, I cannot say at what exact time, we arrived before the locality of Djevrska." Paragraph 8: "At approximately 2100 hours, I'm not sure exactly at what time, it could have been a bit earlier or even sometime later, I entered Djevrska with the commander of my company, Mr. Josip Elez, Mr. Ratko Despot, Mr. Miljenko Zivkovic, the late Zivko Baric, and two conscripts. The conscripts were with us because the company was partially comprised of conscript soldiers. Vladimir Gojanovic was not with us. There were seven of us." At paragraph 10: "During the aforesaid period, and for the whole period of the operation, I do not recall Vladimir Gojanovic. I'm sure that he was not with us in Djevrska because I'm sure that seven of us were there, whom I listed previously." My question to you, Mr. Gojanovic, is: Is it possible that, in fact, you were not in Djevrska with six other people on the night of the 5th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is not possible, and we were seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that the last two statements be marked for identification, pursuant to the procedure you outlined on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document ID number 1D22-0380 becomes Exhibit D206, marked for identification. Document 1D22-0402 becomes Exhibit D207, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, I'd like to turn your attention to paragraph 22 of your 2005 statement. In paragraph 22, you talk about tractors and equipment that was gathered in Bribirski Knezovi barracks. You say: "There was ..." -- it should say: "This was scandalous because members of the 113th Brigade, with the knowledge of the command, were taking this material for their own use which shamed the Brigade and the HV. I knew this because of rumours amongst the 113th." Now, I'd like to show you a document, Mr. Gojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is also going be in sanction because I noticed over the weekend, Your Honour, there are attachments to the document that we had originally uploaded into e-court that were not uploaded. So we were in the process of putting it in e-court; but for now we use Sanction and have a hard copy for the witness in Croatian. Mr. Registrar, this will be document 1D22-0388.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is, Mr. Gojanovic, a war booty report, dated 27 August 1995, from Commander Kotlar of the 113th Brigade, reporting to his superiors, and I'll read the first paragraph. It says: "Subject: War booty report." It is addressed to the Command of the Split Military District, Operative Group West: "According to the order of the commander of the Operative Group West, date 23 August 1995, regarding the collected amounts of war booty, we inform you about the collected and registered amounts as follows:" Then it indicates there is an appendix with attachments 1, 3, 4, and 5. If you could scroll through the attachments and take a look at what is in the appendixes, in terms of booty, please, and let me know when you are finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, we will scroll through here for the benefit of the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you see the type of equipment that is being reported there: Gun, bullets, computer equipment, telescopics. My question to, Mr. Gojanovic, is: In your statement --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tractors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... one. One. Sorry, two. My question to you, sir, is: You say in your statement: "I knew this because of rumours." You didn't actually know or you never actually saw what was being stored at the Bribirski Knezovi barracks, did you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this exhibit be marked and tendered and I tender it. Obviously, it is not in e-court yet, but we will get it in e-court hopefully today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just, Mr. Misetic, the relevance is the type of --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The relevance is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- war booty, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And that it was being registered, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, yes, that this war booty was registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D208.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D208 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Turning to my next topic, Mr. Gojanovic. In your statement, you discuss seeing the killing of a prisoner of war. You discuss stopping an attempt to set fire to a house with an elderly lady still inside. You discuss preventing soldiers -- or I should say stopping soldiers who were discussing raping two women who were in a house. My question to you is: Did you ever report any of these incidents to a superior officer?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never reported that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you report it to the military police?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never reported that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: From 1995 until today, have you ever reported it to an organ of the Republic of Croatia, whether civilian or military?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that the only institution that you've ever reported what you saw is to this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the public. If I may, I can clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Namely, as the chairman of the association, I gave a public statement, including the topic on war profiteers, and it angered a lot of people who are now complaining against my testimony. And in that sense, I believe that I have informed the public, not in as specific details as The Hague Tribunal, but I informed them about the events during the Operation Storm, and I'm not just hiding behind my words.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: With respect to the three specific incidents that I discussed, have you ever publicly stated that you were a witness to these events, to these specific events?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: My final topic area, Mr. Gojanovic, the burnings in Kistanje [Realtime transcript read in error "Kiseljak"] which you say you saw, and you were asked some questions about that by the Prosecutor. If I could take you to your statement, which is paragraph 13 of your statement, the 2005 statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm advised, Mr. Registrar, I don't know with if this will be corrected in the record later, but page 17, line 21, the town referenced is "Kiseljak," and it should be "Kistanje."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 13, you discussed the events in Kistanje. In the second sentence, you say : "When we entered the town of Kistanje, there was already a Croatian military presence, and the 4th Guards Brigade had already been through the town. We were told that by the Croatian army in Kistanje." Further down towards the middle, you say: "I later learnt, from someone in the 142nd Brigade, that the SIS men from the 113th Brigade torched the post office in Kistanje, which was a ridiculous act." My first question to you, sir, is: Mr. Petric was a member of the 13th [sic] Home Guard Brigade Regiment, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interpretation is not quite correct, concerning the 13th Regiment. The word in Croatian was not quite correct, so I can't really quite understand what it is that you asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petric was a member of the 15th Home Guards?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of that. Those are his personal military data.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, are you aware that Mr. Petric and the 15th Home Guards were in Kistanje on the 5th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know during the -- I learned this during the period after the operation, because during the Operation Storm, Ivica Petric and I did not know each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. But you learned this information from Mr. Petric because you sat in on Mr. Petric's interview by the Office of the Prosecutor, where Mr. Petric said, in 2002, that he was a member of the 15th Sibenik Home Guard Regiment, and that he was in Kistanje on the 5th of August. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're alluding to that, namely, that I heard this information from Ivica Petric during the proceedings or work with the The Hague investigators, that's not true, because I know for a fact whom I had heard it from. I think that one does not need to respond to a rumour of that extent. However, it is of such a nature that one needs to tell the The Hague investigators about the situation in Kistanje on that day and that it is based on a rumour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Are you aware today, regardless of whether you heard it after Operation Storm or during Operation Storm, that Mr. Petric was in Kistanje on the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you wish to ask whether I know about that fact right now? Well, I knew about that even before these proceedings, but not during the Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Then that leads me to my next question, Mr. Gojanovic, which is: In giving your statement at paragraph 13, and in giving your testimony in court on Friday, why didn't you mention the 15th Home Guard Regiment or Mr. Petric being present in Kistanje on the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody asked me about that, like you asked me about it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, you have no proof that the 4th Guards Brigade was ever in Kistanje, do you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't have evidence of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Misetic. Ms. Higgins, you're on your feet. May I take it that you will cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Gojanovic, you will now be cross-examined by Ms. Higgins, who is counsel for Mr. Cermak. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Gojanovic. I'd like to take you straight away to the first statement that you made on the 20th of January 2005 which you have been looking at. Now, at that time that you made that statement, you confirmed that it was true to the best of your knowledge and recollection. Do you agree? Do you agree, Mr. Gojanovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And you knew that when you made that statement, you -- the statement itself may be used in legal proceedings and that you may be called to testify before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Let me take you straight away to the relevant part for my purposes of your statement which is paragraph 13, if you can have that before you. It states as follows: "I also learned later that all the equipment and machinery from the factory in Kistanje was taken by a detachment of men acting under the orders of General Cermak. This is stupid because we were capturing the area and the factory would have provided employment for our people; but in this way, all the money went to the generals and we, the liberators, got the blame. Based on what I was told, they used military trucks to take the things from the textile factory; and when Cermak arrived, he chased all the soldiers that were checking it away, cordoned it off, and began loading the equipment on to military trucks. I learnt this later from someone in the 142nd Home Guard Brigade, and that it happened sometime after my unit had left the area." Now, that was your statement in 2005, Mr. Gojanovic; and last week, in the proofing session, if I take you to what you said there, merely this: That you were told that Cermak's people who were infamous arrived and chased the soldiers away and that you were not told that Cermak himself had arrived. Have I stated that correctly?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to you help me with this: Why is it that you said, in your first statement, that Mr. Cermak was not only present but he was chasing, cordoning off, and loading?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used a wrong term. When speaking about Cermak, I actually meant Cermak's men. And the information I received from somebody else, I put it in the correction of my statement from 2005.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Well, let's look at that a little bit more closely, if we may. Now, you were given the chance to correct items in your 2005 statement when you gave your second statement this year, in January 2008. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And you would agree would me, I presume, that it is a very different matter to say that someone was present or that it was, in fact, people present, not being Mr. Cermak. You'd agree that was a significant inaccuracy, I presume? Could you --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Just help me with this: Why is it that you waited until just a couple of days before coming to testify at this Court to make that correction? Why didn't you make it in your second statement?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said a bit earlier, let me explain. When using the word "Cermak," when giving my statements, I had in mind Cermak's men; but when I went back and reviewed my statement, I still took it that in saying "Cermak," I meant Cermak's men. It is an omission on my part that I didn't put it in concrete terms as the situation required.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Just to conclude on that point, you'd agree with me that on a reading of your first statement in Croatian, the meaning is, in fact, that Mr. Cermak was present, chasing, loading. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Higgins, your point is perfectly clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In general, as a guidance, the ritual dances in the beginning, is this what you wanted to tell in accordance with the truth, et cetera, of course, I fully understand that is part of the art of [indiscernible], not always in full extent necessary. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Let me examine the source with you, Mr. Gojanovic. Who gave you this alleged information? Can you give me the name, please?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A member of 142nd provided it to me, and that was after the year 2000. It was done in the work of the association that I have been leading for eight years now. His name is Miro.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, why didn't you provide that name prior to just now? Why didn't you tell the Prosecution and give that detail, if that's correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because, as chairman of the Croatian Association, I have the duty to protect the interest of Croatian demobilised defenders.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Well, you also have a duty to come before this Court and provide truthful and accurate information of which you are aware. So I'd like to ask you if you can provide with his address please because I'd like to make contact with this individual.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the address of this person because the association is such -- has such a system of work where the president has contact with people without having to know their addresses.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Where were you when the conversation took place? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Right now, I can't remember that, I can't recall, because it's been a long time. However, the fact remains etched in my memory, and I wanted to use that fact to clarify to The Hague investigators the situation that was described in rumours circulating at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Well, can you help me with when he told you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After 2000, but I couldn't tell you in more detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may suggest, I'm sorry to interrupt, if the witness has any further information on this other person, perhaps we could go into private session and maybe the witness might --

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may just address that briefly. The witness has come here to testify with no protective measures. He is not able to provide with me any details to date that I would wish to be written down if it he were appropriate to do so. So we're not there, and I'm asking perfectly proper questions to test the reliability of this witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, the witness heard this morning from the witness [sic] about what he describes as perfect directions to the first portion of his evidence, which is a matter the Chamber might want further to look into and might also have consequences of what to do in private session, what not to do in private session. Therefore, with full respect for the public character of this hearing, let's proceed at this moment; but, at the same time, this may be some reason for pursuit. At this time, I think, Ms. Mahindaratne, this has no direct practical consequence for the questions Ms. Higgins has put to the witness until now. If there's any moment, Ms. Higgins, where in view of my earlier observation you would consider, that this might be a moment for caution that you take matters so slowly as to give an opportunity to Ms. Mahindaratne to respond or even for the Chamber to intervene when necessary. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: How did the conversation come about, Mr. Gojanovic? How did it come about that you were talking with this man about a factory in Kistanje? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The work of the association, which I have been leading for years, includes a number of types of communications about the activities which took place during the war and after the war. And in that sense, the primary task of the president of the association and the association itself is to protect the interests of all demobilised defenders, regardless of how difficult are the circumstances in which these defenders find themselves nowadays.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: If can you answer my question, which is this: How did it come about the circumstances that you and this individual were talking about a factory in Kistanje? I understand the role of your association, but that's not my question.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are asking me about the very specific circumstances of that conversation, I simply do not recall them right now. If you are asking me about very general circumstances about that conversation, then I have already provided the answer to you through my previous answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, the question clearly is: Why did you deal with this subject in your conversation with this person? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're asking me about what prompted me to talk to him. Well, what prompted me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to talk with him, but what prompted you to talk about this subject? Did he raise the matter, did you raise the matter? What made you discuss this matter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, that person initiated the subject himself based on newspaper clippings of articles that were published during the Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... tell that you he had any personal knowledge of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Higgins.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: These newspaper clippings and articles, presumably he would have handed those into the association. Do you have those?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically about the incident we're talking about now, I don't have the newspaper clippings, but I believe they are available on the Internet, if they are still kept on those web sites.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Where can I find them, Mr. Gojanovic? Perhaps you can help me.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the Internet, among the archives of various newspapers in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Which web sites?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Web sites of Croatian newspapers: Jutarnji List, Slobodna Dalmacija, and others. I suppose it is there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: They are not in your own archives, are they, just to be clear?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they're not.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Let's talk about the factory, shall we? You've been through Kistanje? Can you tell me what the factory looked like, first of all, please?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the factory anymore because I don't remember the passage through Kistanje, as such, anymore. My statement is linked to what another person remembered. I don't recollect what the factory looked like anymore.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Well, do you recollect how many factories there were in Kistanje?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, but from what I learned after the war, Kistanje had only one factory.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: What do you say the factory made?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in my statement, when I was giving it, I didn't even know what the factory produced, whether it was producing metal screws or clothing. And when I was giving my statement, I didn't even know what kind of factory it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Gojanovic, isn't it correct that, in fact, there are only two factories in Kistanje? One is a factory of specialised tools that was part of the Tvik factory in Knin, and the second was a metal company, a metal factory called Jadran. Does that ring a bell by any chance?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Well, the only textile factories are actually or were actually in Evonik and Knin, not Kistanje. Does that help you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have already stated, in the statement that I gave to the OTP, that I didn't know what this factory manufactured; therefore, I think your question is pointless because I have already replied indirectly to any follow-up question on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Let me move on to a question which I hope you find is not pointless, and that's dealing with the people that you say you were told were involved. Now, in your first statement in 2005, you described them as a detachment under the orders of General Cermak. In your second statement, just to remind you, there's no mention of the incident at all. And in your proofing sheet last week, within the last few days, you used the term merely "Cermak's people, who were infamous." Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who were those people. I don't know them personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: How many of them?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, probably from Zagreb, because General Cermak was mostly stationed before Operation Storm in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: How many trucks?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Where had the trucks come from? Do you know any detail about that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Your Honour, bearing in mind what you said earlier, I'd like to move into private session for a very short period please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I, finally, want to ask you to look with me at a series of four documents which I'm going to put before you, show to you, and then I will ask you a question. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Can I ask, Mr. Registrar, for the document 2D02-0039 to be pulled up on to the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Gojanovic, this is a document dated the 10th of August, 1995; and in the top right-hand corner, you can see a stamp marked "Received," and it is from Major Ivan Juric, to the head of the military police administration, which you can see from the context of the document. I'm going to read into the record a very short extract at paragraph 2, if you could follow please: "In the zone of responsibility of the 4th General Military Police, Sibenik Company, its members, beside regular military police tasks, are still guarding two industrial facilities and the Orthodox monastery in Kistanje." Can you follow that with me, Mr. Gojanovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, can I ask now for the second in this series of four, dated the following date, the 11th of August, 1995. It is document 2D02-0043 to be put on to the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, just reading again, you will see, again, that it is from the same series. It is from the same individual, Major Juric, to the head of the military police administration. And this time, I'm going to read into the record, and if you could follow, paragraph 1, starting on the second line: "It is expected that during the day MUP, Ministry of Interior members, will take over the security in Kistanje (around Elovac monastery, Jadran factory, and Tvik factory). Points in security in Drnis are unchanged."

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: If we could now move to the third in the series, which is, in fact, a 65 ter, which is 01741, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Again, same individual, same format, paragraph 1, line 1: "On the 12th of August, in the zone of responsibility of the 4th General Military Police Company, Sibenik, members of the MUP have not yet taken over the security in Kistanje around Elovac monastery, Jadran factory, Tvik factory."

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And, finally, if I can ask for 65 ter 02048, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Same format, 13th of August, paragraph 1: "In the zone of responsible of the 4th General Military Police Company, Sibenik, members of the MUP took over the security in Kistanje, around Elovac monastery, Jadran factory, Tvik factory." Do you see that, Mr. Gojanovic, from the documents?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Have you seen any of these documents prior to your proofing sessions or in the sessions that you had when you made your statements?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Can you see that, in fact, these documents show that the two factories in the monastery in Kistanje were, in fact, guarded, it appears, by the 4th General Military Police from before the 10th of August?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And that the --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Yeah, sorry. Carry on, Mr. Gojanovic.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still can't see which dates are concerned because I can see in the heading 13th of August, and here, in pencil, it is written 11th of August; whereas, you are asking me whether I can see from the document that members of the 72nd battalion, if I understood correctly, had taken over these factories before the 10th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Gojanovic, I have taken you through the documents, I have read out the relevant passages, and my assertion remains that the guarding of the factories was, in fact, in accordance with what I have read out. That is merely what I'm trying to establish with you, Mr. Gojanovic.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that. I see from these documents that that is the case, but I hadn't seen these documents before.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I understand that. I have no further questions for you, Mr. Gojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: But I would ask that the two documents which are not 65 ter in that series be admitted as exhibits in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you please assign numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Document ID 2D02-0039 becomes Exhibit D209. Document ID 2D02-0043 becomes Exhibit D210.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then D209 and D210 are admitted into evidence. Just for the record, Mr. Gojanovic, you said the document mentioned, in handwriting, the 11th of August. It appears that that is the 11th of August of 2004, rather than of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can I make one further clarification, Your Honour, which is I also seek, although they're 65 ters, the last two documents - that's my mistake - I also seek admission of those, please, the full series of four. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The full series of four, then we need two additional numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, 65 ter number 01741 becomes Exhibit D211, and 65 ter number 02048 becomes Exhibit D212.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D211 and D212 are admitted into evidence. Please proceed. Yes, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do not know exactly how much time you would need, but I take it more than five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, a bit more than five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll first have a break, and we'll then proceed after the break. Mr. Gojanovic, we'll have a break for 25 minutes. After the break, you will be cross-examined by Mr. Mikulicic, who is counsel for Mr. Markac. We will resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Gojanovic.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I'm Goran Mikulicic, Attorney-at-Law, representing General Markac in this trial. I will be putting questions to you, and please provide answers to the best of your recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registry please bring up on the screen 1D22-0362, and could we zoom into the upper left portion on this page.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: There are several microphones on in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, can you see it on the screen? Can you see the article entitled, "The state top is responsible for genocide in Varivode and Gosici"?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This is the article published in Vjesnik Daily on 16th of September 2004?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Another article in the same paper was already put to you earlier, but I will discussing this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: For the sake of the record, the article reads as follows: "The Republic Organisation of the Croatian Association of Demobilised Defenders from the Homeland War sent to the Chief Prosecutor in The Hague, Carla Del Ponte, a request to hold a meeting urgently in order to turn over to her documents; that is to say, evidence proving the involvement of the then-state top in the Varivode and Gosici case when, in 1995, ten civilians of Serb ethnicity were called."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, 18, I apologise. In paragraph 2, it reads as follows: "Based on the documents collected, Gojanovic accuses for the crimes, Franjo Tudjman, Ivan Jarnjak Gojko Susak, Miroslav Separovic, Mate Ganic, Nikica Valentic, all the way up to Ivica Racan, Sime Lucin, and Ingrid Anticevic-Marinovic, who allegedly concealed the evidence of ethnic cleansing in Varivode and Gosici." The last paragraph reads: "When asked why he disclosed the documents to the public not long after the county branch of the Croatian Democratic Party Had ordered the eviction of the association from the premises that he this used so far, Gojanovic said that it was only now that they had collected the documents." My question, Mr. Gojanovic: The contents of this article, do they reflect accurately what you said to the journalist Ana Rukavina.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The late Ana Rukavina, and my answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could this document be tendered into evidence, please, and assigned a number.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is Exhibit D213, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D213 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will now ask the registry to call up Exhibit 3D00-0685.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This document represents the minutes from the session of the Government of the Republic of Croatia, held on the 5th of October, 1995. The session was attended and, in fact, it was chaired by the then-prime minister, Nikica Valentic, and then the attendees are listed. Following that, the ministers that were present and those were absent. Do you see the document, Mr. Gojanovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could we now turn to page 2 of this document where we see the agenda for the session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Under item 2 of the agenda for this session of the government, it reads: "Information on the killing of nine civilians of Serb ethnicity in the village of Varivode."

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could we now turn to page 8, which is 3D00-0692.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Here, we have the summary of the information, where it says: "The minister of the interior, Ivan Jarnjak, informed the government on the killing of nine civilians of Serb ethnicity in the village of Varivode near Knin, noting that all of them were elderly and that they were killed with a fire-arm. "Ivan Jarnjak also informed the government on the measures taken by the Ministry of Interior, aimed at identifying the perpetrator of this crime as soon as possible." Then it says that there was a discussion concerning this item.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could the registry now -- or rather, could the this be admitted into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The one thing I asked myself, Mr. Mikulicic, is no questions have been put to the witness in relation no document, has it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will put my questions when we look through the whole documents that I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So questions still to come. Then, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D214, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D214 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registry now please call up 3D00-0624. While we're waiting, by way of explanation, Your Honour, this is a document that we uploaded into the e-court, but this document hasn't yet been translated officially by CLSS. In order to be of assistance, we translated the part of the document that we wish to put to the witness; and, whereby, we translated the first document. The second document is a transcript of the government session that has a total of 53 pages. We requested that the entire document be translated; but for the purposes of today's witness, we will be only using a part of the document which starts on page 3D00-0661. Could the registry please put on the screen 3D00-0661.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In the discussion on the second item of the agenda, about the killing of civilians in the village of Varivode, Mr. Ivan Jarnjak, the then-minister of the interior, took the floor and said as follows: "Mr. President, on Friday in Varivode, it was established that in that village nine persons, all of them of Serbian ethnicity, all nine of them elderly, were killed."

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the following page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will now read the section that starts in the middle of the page with the words "We undertook ..." "We undertook preventative measures, which means that we used much stronger forces to block all roads and trails, which is exceptionally difficult because this is a region where there are many of these small trails that can be very easily and quickly traversed by off-road vehicles, and this makes the situation very difficult for us. But it is certain that, in several days, we will release all names accompanied by solid evidence, and then we will send an open letter, a general letter or a letter of a general nature, to the public prosecutor."

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the following page, please, the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Minister Jarnjak goes on to say: "Therefore, this is no longer an issue of some folklore. There is now an issue of serious organised crime that we are blamed for and which we have to resolve. We will attempt to resolve it; however, I say that we are seeking ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The following page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: "... greater involvement of civilian authorities."

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now turn to page 3D00-0665. The last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Here, Prime Minister Nikica Valentic took the floor, and said as follows: "Before I start the discussion, Deputy Prime Minister Granic has already asked to speak and we cannot start the discussion now as there is no time, and we cannot discuss the general security situation in the country, especially in occupied territories. But, here, for the sake of the record and for the sake of my own responsibility, I wish to say as follows: A state in which civilians are killed, regardless of who they are, a state that is unable to intervene ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then the continuation it on the following page. Could I see the following page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: "... a state that is unable to protect civilian, that state, that country, has no chance of achieving the goals that we are supporting. It is completely understandable to me that there are all kinds of things, that there is revenge, that there is violence, that there is greed, but we have to give the utmost importance to this issue. "I talked about this most seriously with the president of the state, who is the only one who has power in that respect because he has powers over the army staff, and the government does not have any formal or factual powers. Therefore, I will personally say, and I will say this in any other situation, that I will have no peace, I myself, personally, until the perpetrator is identified and punished." Mr. Gojanovic, my question: Having read the minutes of the government session where one of the items on the agenda was this murder that you testified about, I am asking you this: Were you aware of this position of the then-Croatian government and authorities in the broader sense of the word?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for this political position stated publicly at the cabinet session of the Croatian government, I didn't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Again, I take it that the witness doesn't know anything about it. What then? Is it just for to us know what he doesn't know about or what is it? Is it the suggestion that what is said here was actually the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... it's opposite to his statement in the newspaper article which we were providing at the beginning of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness says, to a newspaper, the government looks guilty, and the government, apparently in an internal document of which you have read only part, not the portions about "We will go after the perpetrators," but there are problems. You just select your own part of it. Well, there is no objection from the other side. But just for you to know, that, of course, the Chamber will look at it, not necessarily only to the portions you quoted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I selected only portions due for the value of the Court's time. That was the only reason, and you will find out afterwards that the other portions of these minutes are not relevant for the subject of the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But also the portions that were translated give other information about the investigations and about perpetrators as well. That's also portions which did you not read. There are no objections. Then, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this becomes Exhibit D215.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D215 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And my last subject, Mr. Gojanovic. You have turned over to the Court today one set of documents you received over the weekend, and you want them to be considered. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You turned over a certificate issued by the defence department from Sibenik, from which it transpires that you were mobilised on the 3rd of August and demobilised on the 7th of May, 1995 -- sorry, 7th of September, 1995. You also turned over a letter, a reply by Mrs. Carla Del Ponte to your letter. I'm not interested in that for the moment. Among other things, you turned over a copy of your army service book: One that was previously valid but has been cancelled, and the current one.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that anywhere, in these documents, it is stated that you were a member of 113th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, and I'll tell you very specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that everyone, meanwhile, has hard copies of these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you can see, Counsel, on page 21 of my old army service book --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- it is clearly stated that it was issued by the department of defence, and it says I have to immediately report to military unit 9025/33, to the assembly point Slime, Jadrija in Sibenik district.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I can see that, Mr. Gojanovic, and others in the courtroom have had opportunity to see it as well, but my question was: Do these documents refer anywhere to the 113th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And since you come from Croatia, have you ever seen a reference to any military unit by name in any army service book? There is usually a reference to the number of the military unit, and this is a military secret. The army service book is a military secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I suppose you have asked for a waiver of military secret when you turned over these documents to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: President, just one point, the documents were not turned over to the Prosecution but to Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You didn't receive a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I just wanted to point out that the documents were brought to the Court by the witness and not before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, how are we going to deal with these documents? Questions were put to the witness in relation to his military booklet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I address the Court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... dealing with the procedural aspect of it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had a discussion during the break about these documents; and, basically, the Defence -- neither the Defence nor the Prosecution has any objection to the Court admitting the documents presented by the witness. The only caveat is obviously, that I think goes without saying, is that we'll take -- we will research the documents; and if this is an problem with them in any way, we will bring it to the attention of the Court after we have an opportunity to seek confirmation that these are authentic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber suggests that we admit these documents, the bundle as a whole, as a Court exhibit, since it has been offered to the Court and since the parties do not object against it. Mr. Registrar, the bundle, which exists of copies sent by fax, apparently on the 18th of May 2008; copies of a document dated the 3rd of September, 1999, apparently about service of Vladimir Gojanovic in the period of between the 3rd of August and the 7th of September, 1995. That's one document in the bundle. The second document appears to be a military booklet, an old one, that has been annulled. The third document being another military booklet concerning this document. Now, the then remaining document is the letter sent by the former Prosecutor of this Tribunal, Carla Del Ponte, to Mr. Gojanovic, 18th of November, 2003. It is not exactly clear what the relevance of this document is. Mr. Gojanovic, could you add one word why you added this to your military documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll be very brief and specific. Last Friday, at the last session in this trial, the Defence practically accused me by saying that my participation here as a witness is somehow related to the work of my association and the eviction of our association from its premises in Croatia. But, here, in the last paragraph of this letter, I draw your attention to the words of Carla Del Ponte, about the real motivation that drove us when we presented all the documents to the OTP, together with two DVDs. I would appreciate it, Your Honour, if you would allow me personally to read that sentence regarding the motives. May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the document will be admitted into evidence, the Chamber can read what is in the document; and, therefore, there is no need to read it at this moment. I do understand that you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's just one sentence, please. Just once sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... aware that it is just one sentence. I do understand that you consider this document relevant for what Ms. Del Ponte has written to you. That's sufficient. Thank you. Mr. Registrar, the whole bundle existing of four documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This becomes Exhibit C2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, on Friday, you were shown a statement given to the Gotovina Defence team by one Dragan Rak, who the Defence suggested was the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 113th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: For the record, I'm referring to the statement D197, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In that statement, Dragan Rak claims that in he knew you, because you had served your compulsory service in the 113th Brigade in 1992 and 1993. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because that is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In fact, the Defence suggested to you that you had served your compulsory service in the 113th Brigade before joining the 4th Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: For the record, transcript reference number 3038.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now my question to you is --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I call up in the meanwhile document D190, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently, one of your previous questions caused some confusion because he did in the ask whether he recalled that statement to be read to him but whether he recalled, which is ambiguous because do you recall the statement or do you recall what was in the statement, and therefore the witness said that it was not true. But I take it that he may well have recalled the statement being read to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. I will move on; although, I do not want to waste any further time on that. May I call Document D190.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, did you know a person by the name of Dragan Rak any time before Operation Storm or during Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, as I just mentioned, the Defence, in fact, suggested to you that you had served your compulsory service in the 113th Sibenik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now if we could just move on to page, in the English version, page 4. That is the document which bears number 1D22-0375.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, on the screen, Mr. Gojanovic, is one of the disciplinary measures ordered, tendered by Mr. Misetic. And if you see in the main paragraph, it's recorded as this: "Vladimir Gojanovic, soldier rank, who is serving in VP 3134 Sinj, 1st Battalion, 2nd Company." Do you not that? Mr. Gojanovic, do you note that reference? You're not getting translation?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The date of this document is 10th September 1993. Do you note that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Was this disciplinary measure meted out to you during your compulsory service?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
