utterances.text: Now, in fact, when Mr. Misetic suggested to you that you had served your compulsory service in Sibenik Brigade, you did say that your compulsory was served in the Sinj area. Do you recall that? Do you recall that statement?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that, and that's the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now while we're on this document, if we could move on to the next page. That is the disciplinary measure dated 8 September 1994. That is document bearing ID 22-0377. I think that is page 6. We're on the wrong page. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, this disciplinary measure or order is signed by Commander Kotlar. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it is signed by -- the document I have here is 8 September 1994. It is signed by Commander Kotlar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can't see whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Krsticevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- what is on our screen at this moment, both what --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Damir Krsticevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It says "Brigadier." I'm sorry. I mentioned the wrong name.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Brigadier Damir Krsticevic, now he was the commander of the 4rd Guards Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And in that page, there is a paragraph which -- with the subheading, "Legal Remedy." Do you note that? Can you please look at the screen, Mr. Gojanovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... stated: Against this order, an appeal may be filed to the commander of the Split Military District within three days from receipt or notice." Now, during your time in the 4th Guards Brigade, are you familiar with persons appealing to the Split Military District command against disciplinary measures? Did you know of incidents, and I'm not talking about yourself. Perhaps, are you aware of incidents where your fellow soldiers may have appealed to the Military District command?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other soldiers, too, were involved in similar incidents, and I know for sure that nobody ever appealed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Moving on, may I call up document number ID 220329. This has not been tendered in evidence. It is one of the Defence documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, while the document is being brought up -- it is before you. Do you recognise this document, Mr. Gojanovic? This is your personnel record obtained by the Defence, in fact, from the HV mobilisation office. Do you recognise this? This is your record, the record relating to you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recognise it because I had never had access to these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your name is recorded at the top of the document as "Gojanovic, Vladimir," and your personal details are recorded there. Is your date of birth correct there, 25th February 1972?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you testified that your compulsory service was not in the 113th Brigade but in Sinj. Then you went on to say that, after Sinj, you served in Zagreb and then in Delnice before you joined the 4th Guards Brigade. Do you recall saying that to the Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, and that's exactly so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can we move on to page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you note under paragraph numbered 14 which says "Service Period," you have your service recorded from 16th August 1993 to 22nd October 1993 as being in Sinj, unit identified as 3134; and from 2nd February 1994 to 1st March 1994, you are recorded as serving in Zagreb; and from --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, Mr. President. That was 23 October 1993 to 2nd February 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And then from 2nd February 1994 to 1st March 1994 in Delnice; and then from 1st March 1994 to 16th June 1994, you're recorded as having served in the Split, that the 4 Guards Brigade. That's correct, isn't it, that's what you testified when you were

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was my statement. But I notice an error here concerning the military post box in Split. It was in year 1995. It was the 16th of June 1995, the end date.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE
utterances.text: If you go on further down, if you see paragraph number 21 which has a subheading, "Service during the war," you're recorded as having served in the Split 4th Guards Brigade up to 6th March, 1995. That's when you were demobilised from 4th Guards Brigade. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE
utterances.text: And then just below that, there is a record that you have served from 3rd August 1995 to 7th September 1995 in a unit identified as 9125- --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm going object, Your Honour, to the use of the word that he "served." It simply notes when the mobilisation order date and the demobilisation order date. Whether or not he served is not reflected in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Service during the war" reads, and perhaps you put it literally, "war unit 9125-33," but, at the same time, illegible and crossed out, "from the 3rd of August until the 7th of September, 1995." Let me just look at this. Whether or not he served, Mr. Misetic, I read under 21 "Service during the war." To say that the document doesn't say anything about this is not completely understood by me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is active military service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we see there 21, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. But if you look in the original, off on the right, on the first entry for Split --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the original? Yes. But your objection was not that comparing with the original that you find different matters. You said that it didn't say anything about service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What I was referring to, Your Honour, if you look at the original on the first entry, it says "DVD," which in Croatian means [B/C/S spoken], which is "active military personnel." The same entry is not made on the second line, which is what my objection was based on, Your Honour. However, on the pro forma, the form section, it does say that; however, in the handwritten entry, there is a distinction between whether he was active or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's ask the witness. It is not a simple issue. It is suggested, Ms. Mahindaratne, that you precisely point to the witness what the portion is, what it says, and what your question is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, let me draw your attention to paragraph 21, which reads: "Service during the war." Now, this is a unit identified as 9125/33, and then it says "from 3rd August 1995 to 7th September 1995." Now could you explain to the Trial Chamber as to what that record indicates from what you know, based on your experience in the military?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. You see the military post office box 9125/33, and it is indicated that I was a participant in active operations as part of the 4th Split Brigade in the period indicated. That's when I received the commendation to receive a medal, as Mr. Misetic mentioned, from the Dubrovnik theatre of war; whereas, at that time, I was a member of the 113th Brigade. So it must have been a mistake in record keeping.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... may I just to interrupt. Can you just indicate, don't go into all those details, what does that entry indicate? What does it mean? Just go by exactly what is stated there, if you could explain to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 21 reflects the period during which I participated in the homeland war in military post 9125/33. You asked me about item 21. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE
utterances.text: That's correct. Now, do the dates, 3rd August 1995 to 7th September 1995, correspond to the time you served in the 113th Sibenik Brigade during Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, fully correspond.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE
utterances.text: Now, on the same page at paragraph 24, under "Judicial punishments," there are no entries there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE
utterances.text: Generally, if a soldier had to be apprehended by a military police for not reporting to active duty, for example, what would be the consequences?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there would be a court punishment, or rather, there would be a prison term, and the person would be court martialed if that was the position taken by the authorities of the Republic of Croatia, military authorities.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE
utterances.text: And if that happened would that -- would that court order or judicial proceedings be recorded in these records?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, they would be recorded.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I wish to tender this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P198, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Let me just give a decision on this. P198 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I call document number 1D22-0348.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE
utterances.text: Now, while that is being brought up, Mr. Gojanovic, in the document we just looked at, the unit you served in during the period 3rd August 1995 to 7th September 1995 is identified by the digits "9125/33." That is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE
utterances.text: Now, what we have before you on the screen is an order issued by the minister of defence, Gojko Susak, dated 2nd August, 1995. That is an order calling for full mobilisation of the 113th Sibenik Brigade on 2nd August, 1995. I appreciate you haven't seen this document, but can you confirm that that's the case?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says there, and it is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE
utterances.text: Now, do you note, under paragraph 1, the 113th Sibenik Brigade is identified by the minister of defence by the digits assigned to the unit which is RP 9125 (113 HV Brigade, Sibenik). Do you note that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE
utterances.text: And that is the same number in which, in P198, you're recorded as serving from 3rd August 1995 to 7th September 1995?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I tender this document in evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection from any of the Defence counsel. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P199, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P199 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I call for document 1D22-0355.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, your testimony was that after a period of duty in Donji Srb, you requested for demobilisation; and, in fact, when you

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE
utterances.text: period of a little over a month. Do you recall saying that the Bench?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Now, I appreciate you may not have seen this document or you may have seen this document. This is the demobilisation order signed and sealed by Commander Danijel Kotlar, dated 30th August, and that is the commander of the 113th Sibenik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the document.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: It reads: "Subject: Termination of mobilisation," and it goes on: "We would like to inform you that we have terminated the mobilisation of the military conscript Vladimir, son of Matte Gojanovic, born 1972, soldier from the 3rd Infantry Battalion, of the 113th Infantry Brigade of the HV, in reference to the decision on demobilisation of certain HV units by the Ministry of Defence." The next paragraph reads: "In the HV, as of 3 August 1995 to 7 September 1995, signed and sealed, Commander Danijel Kotlar." Now, this is what you were talking about right along on Friday, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: And you are being granted your demobilisation from the 3rd Battalion of the 113th Sibenik Brigade, in consequence of a decision for demobilisation of certain HV units by the Ministry of Defence. That is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: There is no record of you not having reported to active duty and being apprehended by the military police in this record is there?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object, first of all, to the leading. Second of all, Ms. Mahindaratne is fully aware that the document to the military police is issued four or five days after the date of the document here, so how that could be -- there is no reference to the document that didn't appear until five days after this document was created is, I think, is a bit illogical and misleads the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I withdraw that question and rephase, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Now, this document is it dated 30th August, and you're granted your demobilisation as of 7th September, 1995. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Now, do you recall you were shown a document by the Defence which was purported to be request sent by Commander Kotlar on 3rd September 1995 to the 72nd Battalion of the military police, requesting that certain soldiers, personnel be apprehended which included your name. Do you recall that? You were shown that document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I remember the document, and I have said that I have never seen it before and that I consider it non-existent.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Now, that document was sated 3rd September 1995. So this document before you is dated 30th August, and your demobilisation is on 7th August [sic]. So if, in fact, that document was issued, it was issued in between these two dates --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, if you have --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we have to compare dates, this Chamber is able to count from one to ten and even to 30 if needed. So, therefore, these are the kind of questions --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I will withdraw --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I mean, you are obviously asking for conclusions which the Chamber is perfectly able to make. Apart from that, demobilisation, I take it that you wanted to refer to the 7th of September.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I thought that's what I said, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said 7th of August, and that's how it appears in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I withdraw that last question, Your Honour, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, just for the convenience of the Court, and because it was our error in not having the signature page of the document that she is now referencing, we can put it in Sanction with the seal and signature page, if counsel wishes, just for the record, to use with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I would not call for that document, Mr. President. So, at this stage --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, if we're talking about originals and about stamps signatures, especially with the present situation, it might be a good idea to have as much copies of originals. The same, by the way, would be true, Mr. Misetic, for the long list because I see that there is, although it is signed for being a truthful copy, it certainly is a transcribed copy, the long list of the soldiers in the 113th Brigade, because I see in the similar last page, that it is not entirely clear to me. Usually, if a document is signed and if you make a copy of it, you don't add to that copy that there is a signature, because you see that usually. Now, here we see both. I'm talking about the long list of those who served on the 113th and were opposed for being or receiving --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I don't have the hard copy with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have a look at it, I would like to see the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If could you now explain to me what the issue is, Your Honour, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We see that there a cover page to a long list, in which I have not checked that yet, but where apparently the name of this witness does not appear. Then in the English copy -- no, not in the English copy. At the last page, we find that on the 24th of August, 2006, this was declared to be a certified copy of the original. Yes? You see that with the stamp [B/C/S spoken]. Now, if you look at the previous page, yes, where we have the last portion of the names, yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, at the bottom there, we find both signatures and a statement that it is his signature. I would like to see that in the original because it is not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. We have it. I can put it in sanction for you right now. It is part --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is in e-court, Your Honour. Right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whether that is the original, that is exactly my question: Whether this is the most original version of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, are we referring to D190 or 191.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm referring to the long list, 735 pages.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: 191, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. We have it. On the second-to-last page is the original -- actually, the last page of the original document, which has both the seal and signatures of both Mr. Cupic and Commander Kotlar; and then the next page is simply the seal from the archive of the Croatian state that it is authentic to the original in the archive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. You say this is the most original version of that document that does exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Except for the original in the Croatian state archive, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which, looking at it, would give exactly the same --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not sure -- if there is any question as to authenticity --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not know. The numbering is not always complete. I was putting this question to you because often if you transcribe an original, you say signature, whereas, on the original, you just see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Which is there on the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We see here both, it appears. We see a signature and the word "signature."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In the Croatian document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see "Potpis," which stands for --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't have that, Your Honour. I have a signature line. Underneath, it says "signature" for where to sign, and there's a signature on it. It says "Potpis."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it could be --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The English is a translation obviously of the original with the seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will have a further look at it and see whether any question remains, yes or no. I might come back to you. Yes. You say it says "signature" for where to sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It says -- literally, it says "Potpis."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I just want to make sure we're looking at the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We see here. The reason we're asking is sometimes you have a document where you just see a signature. Sometime, if a document is transcribed, you see written the word "signature." Here, both appear, which could mean that this -- that the word "Potpis" here means where to put the signature --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... correct. That's what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's your interpretation of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I mean, that is our interpretation, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That is clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'm a bit -- yes, it's the original. Let's move on, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Gojanovic, if a soldier is mobilised and he did not report to active duty, would he be able to obtain an order for demobilisation, as far as you're concerned, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to the leading of the question. She's saying he obtained an order for demobilisation. The document, itself, references that fact that pursuant to an order of the Ministry of Defence, there are many demobilisations going on, of which there is an order for demobilisation. But saying he obtained the order, I think, puts words in the document that are not there and from our position is also inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Let me just remove the word "obtained," then, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or refer, perhaps, to the document the witness brought here, which says something about demobilisation as well. That at least is a document the witness has brought to us.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, according to your -- the records you brought which were tendered to Court directly from here, there was a record that your service was between 3rd August 1995 and 7th September 1995. Now, can you tell Court what that is? What is that document that you brought to the Court.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my military service booklet that has records of all facts pertaining to a soldier who serves in the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Now, the dates indicated, the 3rd August 1995 to 7th September 1995, are the exact dates as set out in this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, is there any possibility that the witness is answering on the basis of his military booklet, where, from what I remember, I do not see that date, and that your question was about another document which was not his military booklet. That is the document dated the 3rd of September, 1999? If not, then please tell us where we find the second date, and also perhaps the first one, in his military booklet.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It is not the military booklet I was referring to, Mr. President. You're correct. He was referring to the military booklet. Let me just take him right to the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, I'm referring to your certificate. Do you have a document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we put it on the ELMO. Mr. Usher, could you put this document on the ELMO. I take it, Ms. Mahindaratne, that you would like to talk about this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, you could first ask how the witness obtained this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I'm just trying to see if the previous document was tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It was not.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, how did you obtain this document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my personal document that I received from the military department. It is authentic. It is a copy of the original, which I have in my records at home.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the current period of time --

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Please try to confine your response to my question. Now what is this document? Can you tell the Trial Chamber, briefly, what this document is, just to give the identity of this document.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a certificate of participating in the homeland war during a certain period of time. It was issued by military department of the Ministry of Interior -- or rather, Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia, and it is an authentic document.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Could you just read that first paragraph which starts with what you read. Can you read that out, Mr. Gojanovic? Can you read out the first paragraph of that document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. "Certificate confirming that Vladimir Gojanovic," and then my personal citizen's number, "born on 25th of February, 1972, in Sibenik, residing" and then my address in Sibenik, "participated in the Defence of sovereignty of the Republic of Croatia, in this sense of Article 2, paragraph 1 and 2, on the Law on The Rights of Croatian Defenders from Homeland War, dated 3rd of August 1995 to 7th of September, 1995."

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: And those are the dates recorded in the previous document that we just looked at, 3rd August 1995 to 7th September 1995?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I could not tender the previous document in evidence. That was 1D22-0355, which was Commander Kotlar's order dated 30th August for demobilisation of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see no objections from any of the Defence teams. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. That becomes Exhibit P200.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P200 is admitted into evidence. Could we leave that document for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move into private session for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: While we're on the documents that you brought to Court, may I also ask the registrar to take military book -- booklet, to the witness. Then if you could turn to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have two military booklets, the old one and the new one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The new one, Mr. President. If you could turn to the new one and page 21.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Now, there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, before we spend a lot of time, do all parties agree that the same number that we discussed before appears there, together with Sibenik, Slime, Jadrija, because that's, I think -- and that is the place where he is urgently called to be mobilised, and it is without a date?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Everyone agrees on that. Ms. Mahindaratne, the number is corresponding; no date, place.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can combine that with the remainder of the evidence, unless there is any specific reason why --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I just want to point out the number 9125/33, which relates to the 13th Sibenik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... That's what I said. Yes. Whether it relates to the Sibenik Brigade is another matter, but the numbers are the same and the word "Sibenik" appears. Of course, we have not yet translations. Mr. Registrar, could we request for CLSS that these documents are translated, the documents which have not yet received a number. That's the full set or was it? What was it? Yes, it was C2. A request should be sent to CLSS to have C2 translated, and here again, pages entirely without entries and having same format do not have to be translated 17 times, if the translation then could just mention that another eight, ten, or 12 pages, same format, without entries appear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the reasons expressed earlier by Mr. Misetic, C2 is admitted into evidence, under seal. Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just wanted to point out that P199, actually the letter from the Defence minister, in fact identifies the Sibenik Brigade as "9125."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, without "- 33."

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's not exactly the same, but it comes close to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Moving on, may I call for document 1D22-0145, please.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Now, you testified, Mr. Gojanovic, that you were awarded a medal in 2000 for your participation in Operation Storm; but that since the citation indicated that the participation was for the 4th Guards Brigade, you did not accept it. Do you recall saying that on Friday?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's exactly what I said.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Is this the citation you were referring to? This is dated 27 July 2000, and you are being awarded a medal for Operation Storm. It reads: "For active participation in the preparation and execution of the military police Operation Storm, within that August 1995, for the liberation of Northern Dalmacija, Lika, Kordun, and Banja."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I tender this in evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It says for his participation in the 4th Guards Brigade, and we have no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat it. It does not appear completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: She's read out a portion, and did not read out that he got the medal for his participation in Operation Storm as a member of the 4th Guards Brigade, and it is dated 27 July 2000, so almost five years after the fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I did read the date of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It also does not literally what you say. It gives a name, and it mentioned 4th Guards Brigade. Whether that was at the time of his separation, the place where he was still part of, that is not entirely clear yet. But it is clear that on this document, it appears next to the name, 4th Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I believe we can stipulate that after Operation Storm, 7 September 1995, he was not a participant in the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that means that the puzzle is not yet resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If I may point out that the medal is awarded for his active participation and preparation and execution on the military police Operation Storm. And, within brackets, August 1995, the citation clearly indicates for what period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I see exactly what you want to emphasise and what Mr. Misetic prefers to emphasise. I'm afraid that the Chamber has not yet anything to emphasise at this moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think that document was not given a P number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this becomes Exhibit P201.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P201 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I call for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me again look at this document in detail. It seems that the English translation suggests that the numbers perhaps 1 to 311 are left out, and that the numbers 313 and following do not appear anymore. It is bracket, dot, dot, dot, bracket; whereas, I cannot see that in the original one. At the same time, it would not come as a surprise that the original would list all of the decorated soldiers. Therefore, here again the question arises: Is this the original, the most original, possible. You do not know, Mr. Misetic? You do not know, Ms. Mahindaratne? It adds to the puzzle. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, can you -- based on the documents we've seen, your demobilisation papers indicate you as having served the period 3rd August to 7th September in the 113th Sibenik Brigade; whereas, there is an indication in this citation -- actually, there is an reference to the 4th Guards Brigade. Can you offer an explanation as to this discrepancy?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. I received a decoration for Operation Storm. I was awarded -- in fact, I have to correct myself. I was offered a decoration by the commander of the 4th Split Brigade, Damir Krsticevic, and that paper I received just after the completion of Operation Storm in 2000. A proclamation was published, giving me a decoration for the liberation of Dalmacija, Kordun, Lika, and Banja, but I did not accept the decoration because I had, in fact, participated in liberating the terrain as part of the 113th Sibenik Brigade. I thought it unjustified and improper to receive a medal for something I did not participate in.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Now, did you raise this issue with any of the HV authorities, the fact that this is an discrepancy with regard to the citation?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not raise that at all because I was angry with the shoddiness of the bureaucracy which was completely disorderly and chaotic. And to this day, I did not collect any medal for Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Can you --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I withdraw that, Mr. President. Can I call for document 1D02-0357.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Now, your testimony was that on 4th August, in Pavasovici, one of your colleagues was hit by a bullet and killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm referring to paragraph 6 of his 2005 statement, P194.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: With regard to that issue, the Defence, on Friday, showed you a document, for the record D194, which was a report from Commander Kotlar dated 11 August 1995, according to which the soldier who was killed in Pavasovici on 4th August, namely, Boris Garma, had been killed as a result of a mortar mine, in fact, two metres from where he was. Do you recall the fact that Defence counsel pointed out to you that your version of events differed, in fact, from what was recorded by Commander Kotlar? Do you recall that on Friday Defence counsel pointed this out to you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Now, what we have on the screen here is a report sent to the Split military district by the assist commander for political department of the 3rd Battalion of the 113th Sibenik Brigade, Lieutenant Borislav Slavica, and it is dated 5th August. It relates to the circumstances of the killing of the soldier, Boris Garma, on 4th August. Do you note that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to this document, in the fifth line, it is reported that: "The soldier was hit by a Browning 12.7-millimetre, and remained dead on the spot." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Is that consistent with your testimony, or do you find anywhere in this report any reference to a mortar mine impacting near the soldier?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This bit concerning ammunition is consistent with my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I wish to tender this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit P202.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, P202 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I call document number 1D22-302 -- 0302.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: While the document is being brought up, do you recall, Mr. Gojanovic, on Friday, you were shown two documents by Mr. Misetic, one by General Gotovina and the other by Brigadier-General Kotlar, being ordered to stop illegal activities. Do you recall being shown the documents? I'm not referring to the documents on the screen, but you were shown two other documents on the screen. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember all the documents that have been shown to me by Counsel Misetic.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Then Mr. Misetic asked you if you considered the instance when Commander Kotlar shouted from his vehicle at the soldiers, as an order to stop looting and torching; and you responded in the affirmative. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Now I appreciate you may not have seen this document. Obviously, you have not seen this document, but this is a report from chief of the security information service of the Ministry of Defence, Colonel Ante Gucic; and the information goes to the defence minister and the Croatian reporting service. It is dated 8 August 1995. And in paragraph, it is recorded as this: "In the liberated areas of hinterlands of Zadar and Sibenik, the establishment of the civilian authorities is not being carried out in a satisfactory pace. More precisely, in the liberated settlements Bribirske, Mostine, Djeverske, and Kistanje, the situation is rather chaotic. Incidents of mass burnings of houses, plundering of property, alcohol consumption occur, and the units lack organisation. The reason for such a situation is the insufficient engagement of the command personnel of the units." Now, is that report consistent with your own observations at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, this is misleading the witness. She takes a report from the 8th of August. The two orders I showed him were from the 10th of August and the 12th of August from Commander Kotlar. So, to then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We do know yet what her question is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: She asked the question. She asked: Is this consistent with your observations?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it you suggest that Ms. Mahindaratne breaks down her question to whatever she wants to and specifically asks --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: She started off the question by reminding him that he said that Commander Kotlar had given an oral order, and then asks after showing this document whether that is consistent with his observations. I'm not sure what she means by "observations." But if that is what she is referring to, I think it is unfair to put it out of time sequence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that it is unfair, it might easily confuse the witness and the Chamber. Please be precise in your questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I was referring to the incident of when Commander Kotlar shouted from the vehicle, which is what counsel questioned the witness about, which did not have a time-frame, Mr. President. There is no time-frame as to when --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least the document gives a bit of a time-frame. The question was too general: Does this and this mean what is you said, what we read in the document, and we reed several things in the document. Could you please rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Now, let me actually take to your statement of 2005, P194, and if you look at paragraph 20, Mr. Gojanovic. Could you just look at your statement of 2005. It is in front of you, not on the screen, but you have a hard copy there. There you say this, and let me again just read it to you. Have you found the paragraph?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which page?

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Paragraph 20, about two lines down, third line: "I'm not aware of Commander Kotlar taking any disciplinary measures against any men from his brigade in relation to the looting and burning that was going on. At no time during all the time while I was involved in Operation Oluja, up until the time when I asked to be demobilised, was I or any of the other soldiers in my battalion told that the looting, burning, and other crimes had to stop. I never saw an order that related to the stopping of criminal activities by members of the Croatian armed forces." Now, in the report, which is on your screen, it's recorded as this: "Incidents of mass burnings of houses, plundering of property, alcohol consumption occur, and the units lack organisation. The reason for such a situation is the insufficient engagement of the command personnel of the units." Now, is that consistent with what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne. Have you seen this document before, Witness? Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document on the screen? No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes? No. Now, Ms. Mahindaratne, do you think that if the witness testified about burning houses, and if we find burning houses in a document which the witness has never seen before, whether the Chamber would be in a position to say, Well, at least whether true or not, whether testimony true, whether document true, both of them are talking about burning houses; and to that extent, it seems that it's consistent. But even when I have not been there at that time, I can see that, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I respond, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: My point was, Mr. President, that while Mr. Misetic tried to demonstrate there were orders, in fact, to stop the criminal activity, in fact there is a record from within the institution which indicates to the contrary, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is perfectly clear. The same is true for Mr. Misetic. Mr. Misetic has shown documents which apparently are not fully consistent with the testimony of the witness. Now, it could that be the testimony of the witness is inaccurate, that the orders are inaccurate. We do not know, but they seem not to be consistent. Even if the witness said not one word about that, looking at the document, hearing his testimony, it is obvious there was an inconsistently. That is true for Mr. Misetic, and that is true for your questions as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: For the record, I will make an objection as to what she is using the document for. It is, again, unfair and misleading to then not go into the next paragraph, which defeats - again, I don't want to be argumentative - or which sheds further light on the very assertion that she wishes to put the witness as being consistent with her statement. So if we're going to talk about orders, she needs to put the entire document to the witness then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the question that could come out of that is still something that the Chamber, of course, can see. It might be that the traditional common law procedural approach in how you get information to a jury plays a part here. Perhaps, a jury should be averted that there may be some inconsistency, but here of course the witness sees the document for the firs, the Chamber see it is for the first time. So whether it is consistent or inconsistent is, I would say, rather obvious. That is one thing. Second, if you are seeking an explanation for that, or if the witness could add something to that, or whether the witness is aware of any intentional or by mistake bad reporting, or whether the witness might have had a bad recollection when answering the questions, that's all fine. But the consistency and inconsistency appears from the testimony itself and the document. Ms. Mahindaratne, how much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Just about five minutes at the most, Mr. President, but would not ask any further questions on this document. May I tender it in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Registrar, that would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P203, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In the absence of objections by any of the teams, Exhibit P203 is admitted into evidence. If you could, please, wrap up as soon as possible, so that we can have a break and release the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Will I be allowed to redirect -- recross, I mean? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time would you need for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Less then ten minutes -- less then 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have to do that, then, after the break. Ms. Mahindaratne, if you would finish your re-examination --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, can I do it after the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Let's try to finish within the next three to four minutes with your remaining questions; otherwise, it is split up.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can I call up document 862, please; that is, 65 ter number 862.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: I appreciate, Mr. Gojanovic, that you probably not have seen this document, but you were questioned today on behalf of Mr. Cermak's Defence on the factory in Kistanje. And by this document, Mr. Cermak authorises and entry into a factory.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Do you know which factory that is? Is that one of the factories in Kistanje?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I wouldn't know whether that is the factory.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: This is dated 14 August 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's what's written.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I tender this document in evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just trying to understand what we're talking about. This is a document apparently signed by Mr. Cermak where, on the 14th of August, he gives an authorisation to the Dalmacija Cement, which just looking at the name might be a cement company, to give authorisation to enter the premises of Knin Kips [phoen], which appears to be in are similar area of economical activity because it has been a part of Dalmacija Cement for 20 years. Whether this is any of the -- is there any suggestion that this is one of the factories that we earlier about.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. This is another document. This is to demonstrate that Mr. Cermak did exercise certain amount of control over the factories and properties in the area, and that goes to the issue about on which the witness testified about Cermak's people removing goods from factories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. While I've perfectly understood what you said, that therefore I read the content of this document in quite some detail because this is what the document says. What Ms. Mahindaratne has said about it is her conclusions apparently on the basis of this document. Therefore, I ask whether there was any direct relation to the factories we discussed earlier. This is on the mind of Ms. Mahindaratne. I don't know whether there is any need to express what's in your mind, Ms. Higgins.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I would like to briefly, given that Ms. Mahindaratne has expressed what's on hers, because it has absolutely no relevance at all, Firstly, to the factory in Kistanje issue; but, secondly, this document was one that, in fact, I was going do use with the witness. I chose not to because it doesn't relate specifically to Kistanje. But what it does do is show a role that Mr. Cermak had to try and assist companies who owned or who managed companies prior to Operation Storm to access the buildings, as you can see, to provide for their own security. So it's nothing to do with looting. So I make those comments, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Higgins, by the way, I summarized this document. You might have already have noticed that proper attention was given to the exact text of this document; also that it belonged to a firm before, and for that reason was given access. Well, you have now both expressed your mind. The Chamber is informed about what is on your mind, but the Chamber is, first of all, about what is in the document. Any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: One last question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, one last question.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, it was suggested to you that just one month prior to your interview with the OTP, Office of the Prosecutor, you were evicted from your office in Croatia. Now, can you tell Court as to when you started collecting material with regard to the interview you were seeking with Prosecutor Del Ponte. When did you initially start collecting the material?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you the exact date when we started collecting evidence --

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- underlying the documents we provided to the OTP, but it was a long, long time before the eviction.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, if you could just give the year. I'm not asking for the date, just the year.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it must have been not less than two or three years prior to the eviction, a long time.

utterances.speaker: THE BENCH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That concludes the re-examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness. I apologise to the interpreters and the transcriber for not having taken a break earlier. We will have a break until ten minutes past 12.00, and could I inquire with the other parties whether they would need time for re-examination as well. One second please. I am first inquiring with the other parties.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nothing further. Mr. Mikulicic, nothing further. Mr. Misetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Still 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Hopefully less time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could, yes, please, because then we could have a reasonable amount of time with the next witness. Mr. Gojanovic, you would like to say something? You may briefly address me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I only wish to ask you to ask one question of the Defence team, Mr. Misetic in particular, on my behalf, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, usually the Chamber does not examine Defence counsel. But if there's anything which is on your mind which troubles you, you may not suggest to me that I put questions to the Defence teams; but what is on your mind, what troubles you, you may tell us at the end of your re-examination. So, at the very end, you will have an opportunity to add to your testimony what you like to add. We'll have a break until ten minutes past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, I'd like to ask you to take a look at the picture that is in Sanction right now. It should be on your screen. Do you see a picture of yourself there?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's Mr. Petric to your left -- to your right and to left in the picture?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If you could take a look at the medal your wearing on your upper left hand part of your chest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could blow that up, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is the Operation Oluja medal you received. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't receive it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Are you wearing the Operation Oluja medal in that picture, sir.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, how did you come to wear the Operation Oluja medal?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wore at the time the Oluja medal, just like my fellow soldiers; and when the eviction took place, I wanted to show solidarity with The Association of Croatian Demobilised Defenders, especially being the president of that association.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: My question is, sir: You've testified, I believe on Friday, and you testified now within the last hour, about how you never took the Oluja medal because you were -- it had a false certificate that you were a participant in the 4th Guards Brigade. Now we have a picture of you wearing the Oluja medal, and I would like to know specifically did you accept the Oluja medal for participation in Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Officially, I did not accept the Oluja medal because I received it from the 4th Split Brigade, and I did not participate it in during Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't want to be argumentative with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You asked for it, Mr. Misetic, by using the words "whether you accepted it." You can ask: Did you receive it? Is this your copy? Is this your medal, then why did you wear it? This is the one you received from your, I think, supreme commander. It is your supreme commander who grants the medal, isn't it? Is this the one that you received.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... this, then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. That is it not the medal. This the medal I received from my fellow soldiers who put it on my chest, so that I could protect the dignity of my association when we were evicted by a political party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you used someone else's medal --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in order to underline what you wanted to express at that time. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this be marked and we will upload it into e-court, and I will tender it when it is uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Perhaps, you could give it already a number, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This becomes Exhibit D216, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may, what is indicated there is judicial punishments, and Mr. Misetic is referring to the disciplinary measures, you know, of those documents that were tendered in evidence during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: She opened the issue up, Your Honour. Now the same issue occurred in September of 1995; and now, suddenly, she doesn't think it should be in that section. If she will stipulate to that fact, that's fine with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That was not my point. My point was that judicial punishments and disciplinary measures, there is a difference --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's keep it quite simple. Apparently, this form doesn't say or doesn't give any entry there, neither about disciplinary nor any judicial matter. Some of the decisions I have to check whether it was disciplinary punishment, but at least the salary to be reduced either for one-month percentage, sometimes for two months, has been put to the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... and prison time. He was sentenced to three days in jail as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, therefore, we will consider that all in commendation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I had one question just to tie this up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The question was simply: Do you recall ever being court martialed for abandoning your unit in the years 1993 or 1994?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Turning to my next area, Mr. Gojanovic, you produced a document to us, that was discussed again with Ms. Mahindaratne, signed by Milan Rupic, about your mobilisation in August of 1995. My question to you is: How did Mr. Rupic know whether or not you participated in Operation Storm? Was he a witness to your participation?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Forgive me for objecting, but your question has no meaning because it has to do with the Ministry of Defence of Croatia, which is the only relevant body for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, if you just answer the question. If it is meaningless question, then that goes quickest and the Chamber will find out. May I take it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Yes, may I answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Milan Rupic signed this document. He doesn't need to know whether I participated or not. He simply goes along with the records kept at the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Actually, he is a person in Sibenik, correct, at the defence office in Sibenik?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And my last question to you, sir, is: You were asked as the last question by Ms. Mahindaratne about when you began to prepare the file that you eventually turned over to the Office of the Prosecutor in 2004. I believe your answer was two or three years earlier. Did you begin to prepare this file sometime around after Mr. Petric was released from prison?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Gwaunza was one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: If I could take you back to your first statement, paragraph 10, where you made reference to very young soldiers who are about to set fire to a house in which an elderly women was. Could I ask you what you meant by "very young"?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means they were somewhere around 18 or 19 years of age.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. That's all I wanted to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since the other Judges have no further questions to you, this concludes your evidence in this court. May I take that the question of Judge Gwaunza has not triggered any need for further questions. Yes. You would like to add and I promised to give you an opportunity to add whatever you'd like to add. This Chamber is interested in facts you observed, heard, saw, not in opinions. Please tell us what is still bothering you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I provided my photograph from the military ID to the Court; and in that photograph, I am slimmer. I have about 30 kilos less, and I would like to put a question to Counsel Misetic. Is it possible --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... questions to Counsel Misetic. You are not in a position to put questions to counsel. It is the other way around, that counsel can put questions to you. Thirty kilos less, that is what I'm talking about as well. Tell us what the relevance of this photograph? Which photograph was it? The one that we saw on the screen, or one from your military booklet where the photo on the old one is missing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I have said, that is the photograph from my military ID, and it was taken with me wearing a military uniform, when I was mobilised. My question, if I may put it, has to do with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it possible that statements of soldiers from Operation Storm on Sonkovici-Gracac axis were given, under political pressure, the direct suggestion of Vladimir Vujanovic as chairman, president of The Croatian of War Veterans.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether this is possible or not is a -- usually possibilities, it is not easy to exclude for possibilities whatever has happen, but whether that is a relevant question for the Chamber. If the Chamber receives any documents, statements, just for your information, is that the statements that were put to you have been marked for identification. That means that whether this Chamber will consider them as to the truth of their content is still to be seen. So I'm just explaining a procedural matter to you; that is, they are, as we call it, MFI'd, marked for identification. That means that we know what they are, no further decision has been taken, and it depends on future procedural steps whether other decision would have to be taken. If that answers more or less, may I say, your procedural inquiry, then I would like to thank you for coming to The Hague, for answering all the questions, even for trying to put additional questions. The Chamber wishes you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please follow Madam Usher. Mr. Russo, I see that you appear in this courtroom, which makes me assume that you be the one who examines the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I do understand that the witnesses have to travel a long road in order to get into this courtroom. Madam Usher, could you escort the next witness into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I read a decision. That is a decision -- well, it is not a decision, but reasons for our decision. The Chamber's reasons for granting trial-related protective measures for Witness 69. On the 25th of April of this year, the Prosecution filed a motion requesting that the Chamber order the trial-related protective measures of pseudonym and face distortion for Witness 69. On the 28th of April, 2008, the Gotovina Defence filed a response, in which it did not oppose the request, but disagreed with the Prosecution's arguments in support of a motion. The following day, the Markac Defence filed a joinder to that response. On the 13th of May 2008, the Chamber decided to grant the motion with reasons to follow. This decision can be found at transcript page 2.694. On the 1st of May 2008, the Chamber held, in its reasons for its first protective measures decision in this case, that the party seeking protective measures for a witness must demonstrate an objectively grounded risk to the security or welfare of the witness or the witness's family should it become known that the witness has given evidence before this Tribunal. The mere expression of fear by a witness is insufficient to justify protective measures. This standard can, for example, be satisfied by showing that a threat was made against the witness or the witness's family. Witness 69, a Croatian Serb, lives with his family on his own property in a Croatian village. The Chamber found that the expected testimony of Witness 69 could antagonise certain persons. Furthermore, Witness 69 was visited by a person from Sibenik, possibly a police officer, last year. Another incident in which witnesses in this case were visited by the Sibenik police were brought to the Chamber's attention. In that instance, the visiting police allegedly questioned the witnesses about the statements they had given to the Prosecution for this case, and said that the living relatives of those who been killed would now blame the witnesses for the killings. The Chamber also received information about other potential witnesses being approached by persons claiming to be Croatian police and asked about this case. For the aforementioned reasons, the Chamber finds that the Prosecution has demonstrated an objectively grounded risk to the security and welfare of Witness 69 should it become known that he has given evidence before the Tribunal. That is sufficient to warrant the granting of the requested protective measures which are of a nature to allow the public to understand the substance of the testimony. This concludes the Chamber's reason for its decision to grant protective measures to Witness 69. Madam Usher, could you please escort the next witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Might I be excused, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're excused, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tchernetsky. I apologise that you had to wait for such a long time, but we had to deal with the totality of the testimony of previous witness. I hope that you'll understand this. Mr. Tchernetsky, before you give evidence --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I certainly understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a -- require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. I may invite you to make that solemn declaration, of which the text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tchernetsky. Pleasing seated. You will first be examined by Mr. Russo, who is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and Your Honours. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, would you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY
utterances.text: Alexander Tchernetsky.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you recall giving two statements to the ICTY, one dated the 18th of May 2002, the other dated 6th December 2007?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, Mr. Registrar, if we could please pull up 65 ter number 4877 and 4878.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two at the same time is a bit problematic, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour. In that case, I'll take them one by one. If we could have the first page of the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I take it that you are referring to the May 2002 statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, do you recognise this as the statement that you gave on 18 May 2002?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And is that statement true to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Does that statement accurately reflect what you told the investigators?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if you were examined on those same matters here today, would your answers be the same as in that statement?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY
utterances.text: Yes, but bearing in mind the supplemental information that I provided later.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. We'll move to that next.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. President, if I could have 4877 moved into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. No objections. Then the 2002 statement is - let me just check - is to be assigned a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P204, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And P204 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. If I could now have, Mr. Registrar, please, document number 4878.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is the 6th of December 2007 statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, looking at the screen, do you recognise this as the statement you gave on 6th December 2007?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Is that statement true to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Does that statement accurately reflect what you told the investigators?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, finally, if you were examined on those matters here in court today, would your answers be the same as in that statement?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY
utterances.text: Yes, I would provide identical answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, on that basis, I would move for admission of 4878.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it there are no objections. No objections. Mr. Registrar, that would be number.
