utterances.text: Exhibit P205, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P205 is admitted into evidence. You've got seven minutes left, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will move as quickly as possible. If I could please provide hard copies to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if I could be permitted to read off a very brief summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that you have explained to the witness what the purpose of that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please read it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky was a United Nations Military Observer in Sector South from late June until December of 1995. He was assigned to UNMO Team Podkanje for the length of his assignment in Sector South and became the team leader in October of 1995. Prior to Operation Storm, he participated in daily patrols throughout Team Podkanje's area of responsibility, investigated cease-fire violations by the warring factions, and monitored the safety of the Croatian minorities living in the Krajina. When Croatian forces began shelling the area of Cetina in July of 1995, he and his fellow UNMOs provided an escort for the Serb civilian harvesters in the Cetina area to protect them against further shelling. He also personally experienced the shelling of Strmica by Croatian forces in late July 1995. He was not present in Knin during Operation Storm because he was on leave from approximately 2 to 8 August 1995. In the weeks and months following Operation Storm, he continued on patrols and witnessed acts of looting by HV soldiers and the burning of houses throughout his team's area of responsibility. He also participated in the comprehensive damage survey conducted by all the UNMO teams after Operation Storm and assisted in negotiating the surrender of a group of ARSK soldiers. That concludes my summary, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, I want to try to move quickly through this first subject. Perhaps we can have it done. I would like to discuss first the shelling of the Cetina area in 1995 and the special task that you received called Harvest. And for the benefit, this is explained in his first statement. That is 204 at page 2. Mr. Tchernetsky, do you recall this incident?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY
utterances.text: I recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And in order to assist the Court, I would like you to please locate the area of Cetina on one of the maps you provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: So, Mr. Registrar, if we could please pull up 65 ter 4880.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, do you recognise this map?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Is it one of the maps that you provided to the Office of the Prosecutor with your second statement?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY
utterances.text: Yes. This was my working map at the time, and I saved this copy and I provided it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I would like to tender the entire map as an exhibit and then I'm going to use an enlarged portion of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, none of the other counsel jumps up. No objections. Mr. Registrar, that would be ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry -- Your Honour. The only objection -- I don't have an objection. I just -- I guess if we get a description of what this map is because it is very difficult to read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do we know what the original size of this map is -- yes, that makes it easy to work on it rather than on such a screen. Of course you can blow it up to some extent, but it depends on how intensively we'll use it, but I take it that the witness will be taken to explain what the markings on the map are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. If we could at least know where Knin is on the map and then maybe use that as a reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I could already tell you where Knin is. That is just above P14 and P14. Oh, no, I'm mistaken, that is Denis. I apologise. That is too quick. Mr. Russo will guide us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... whether or not to admit it. Or have we admitted it already. I was about to, no one jumped up, and then Mr. Kuzmanovic jumped. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit P204.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P204 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps if you put one question for the remaining minute, and that is where Knin is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes. If we could enlarge just the sort of centre of the map and move up a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, I realise it is difficult to see on the map here. Are you able to locate Knin on this map, perhaps by the numbers and squares.

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY
utterances.text: Is that question directed to me? I didn't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you could tell us where we find Knin on this map. Perhaps it is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see it here. It's hard to discern.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, I will be providing a hard copy, full size, to the Court as well as the Defence counsel, but I can tell you that the contents of the map are explained in the supplemental witness statement, which is Exhibit P205, at paragraphs 4 and 5. It indicates what the markings on the map are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then that will do for today, I take it. Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Tchernetsky, we are under an iron regime to stop when our morning session time is over, so therefore it is not very pleasant, perhaps, for you to have been called only for 15 minutes, but tomorrow we'd like to continue. We'd like to see you back tomorrow, the 20th of May, at 9.00 in the morning, as far as I'm informed still in Courtroom II. Mr. Tchernetsky, I want to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, especially not the testimony still to be given, because not much of your evidence has been given until now, so therefore you should not speak to anyone about it, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning, 9.00. Then --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's nothing else, we adjourn for the day and we resume tomorrow, the 20th of May, 9.00, Courtroom II.
